basics.name: Siril Teja Dukkipati
basics.label: Postdoctoral Researcher in Spine Biomechanics
basics.summary: Postdoctoral Researcher at MDsim S.A. (Luxembourg), working on clinical validation of the SPINEsim digital twin platform, funded by the FNR (Fonds National de la Recherche, Luxembourg). PhD in Mechanical Engineering (Biomechanics) from McGill University. Research expertise in musculoskeletal modeling, robotic spine testing, 3D-printed spine surrogates, and medical device development.

work.name: MDsim S.A.
work.summary: FNR (Fonds National de la Recherche, Luxembourg) funded postdoctoral research position focused on biomechanical model verification and clinical validation of SPINEsim — a patient-specific digital twin for spine surgical planning.
highlights: Clinical validation of the SPINEsim biomechanical model in collaboration with Prof. Hans-Joachim Wilke, Institute of Orthopaedic Research and Biomechanics, University of Ulm, Germany
Biomechanical model verification and validation (V&V) for Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) regulatory requirements
FNR-funded research bridging computational biomechanics and clinical spine care

work.name: McGill University, Department of Mechanical Engineering
work.position: Course Instructor — MECH 561: Biomechanics of Musculoskeletal Systems
work.summary: Sole instructor for MECH 561 (Fall 2024, Winter 2024). Responsible for full course design, delivery, and assessment covering musculoskeletal tissue biomechanics, force analysis, passive/active kinematics, and clinical orthopedics.
highlights: Full course design and delivery for graduate-level biomechanics course
Topics: musculoskeletal classification, clinical orthopedics, musculoskeletal force analysis, kinematics, experimental methods

work.name: McGill University, Department of Mechanical Engineering
work.summary: Teaching assistant across four courses over five years.
highlights: BIEN 500 — Medical Technology Innovation and Development (Winter 2024)
MECH 262 — Statistics and Measurement Lab (Fall 2024, Winter 2024, Fall 2023, Winter 2023, Fall 2022, Winter 2022)
MECH 290 — Design Graphics for Mechanical Engineering (Fall 2021, Winter 2021, Fall 2020)

work.name: McGill University, MBR Lab
work.summary: Summer Undergraduate Research in Engineering (SURE) fellowship. Implemented and validated the control system for a robotic spine benchtop model.
highlights: Implemented control system on a robotic benchtop spine model
Validated kinematic performance of the robotic model against expected physiological ranges

volunteer.summary: Promoted space exploration and STEM education across South Asia.
highlights: Organized Indian Rover Challenge (IRC) — a national university-level Mars rover competition

courses: Musculoskeletal Biomechanics Research Lab (MBR), supervised by Prof. Mark Driscoll
Bachelor's thesis at R&MM Research Group, Vrije Universiteit Brussel, Belgium

awards.title: GREAT Award — Graduate Research Enhancement and Travel Award
awards.summary: Travel grant awarded for presentation at the 11th European Solid Mechanics Conference (ESMC 2022), Galway, Ireland.

awards.title: SURE Fellowship — Summer Undergraduate Research in Engineering
awards.summary: Competitive undergraduate research fellowship at the Musculoskeletal Biomechanics Research Lab.

publications.name: Evaluation of a Fast-Solving Rigid Body Spine Model Inclusive of Intra-Abdominal Pressure
publications.summary: High-fidelity, fast-solving (1.4 s) MATLAB rigid-body lumbar spine model with 15 DOF, incorporating intra-abdominal pressure. Validated against in vivo literature. Vol. 72, Issue 10, pp. 3108–3119.

publications.name: Design Improvements and Validation of a Novel Fully 3D Printed Analogue Lumbar Spine Motion Segment
publications.summary: Fully 3D-printable L1-S1 spine surrogate with ligaments, validated against cadaveric and FE data. Vol. 21, Issue 3, pp. 1388–1396.

publications.name: Development and Biomechanical Evaluation of a 3D Printed Analogue Lumbar Spine Motion Segment
publications.summary: First reproducible 3D-printable L1-S1 lumbar spine model validated in flexion-extension, lateral bending, and axial rotation.

projects.name: SPINEsim Clinical Validation
projects.summary: FNR-funded postdoctoral project validating the SPINEsim biomechanical digital twin platform at MDsim S.A., in collaboration with Prof. H.-J. Wilke at University of Ulm.

projects.name: High-Fidelity MATLAB Spine Model with IAP
projects.summary: Fast-solving 15 DOF rigid body lumbar spine model inclusive of intra-abdominal pressure. Published in IEEE TBME 2025.

projects.name: 3D Printed Analogue Lumbar Spine
projects.summary: Fully 3D-printable L1-S1 spine surrogate with ligaments. Published in Journal of Bionic Engineering 2024.
